function: Joint sub-band (spectrum) allocation for cognitive UAV links and UAV flying-direction control by deep active inference agents, plus ConvLSTM user-demand prediction (pp. 10-11).
system: Cognitive UAVs at 100 m serve secondary users on 3 sub-bands of 20 MHz shared with primary users; antennas and carrier band not stated; no RIS (p. 11).
method: Deep active inference (policy, value, transformation networks) in a reinforcement-style loop with replay, decentralized multi-agent training; supervised ConvLSTM-attention-DenseNet demand predictor trained offline (pp. 4, 8).
data_channel: Own simulator: LoS air-to-ground gain beta_ref d^-2, Rayleigh ground links; demand from public Milan SMS/call/Internet dataset [36], hourly, 3:1 train/test split (pp. 9, 12).
test_conditions: Training and evaluation in the same scenario (3 PUs, 2 SUs); overlapping PU/SU layout and multi-cell ground network are separate convergence runs, no transfer reported (pp. 12-15).
baselines: Demand: ConvLSTM, ResNet (learned). Allocation: MAPPO, MA2C-DDPG, Q-learning (learned) and random scheme (non-learned) (pp. 12-13).
metrics: Average reward and convergence episodes; SU/PU sum and per-service rates versus demand; RMSE, MAE, R2 for demand prediction; parameters and execution time (pp. 12-15).
complexity: Demand predictor 218,699 parameters, 116.4 ms forward pass (Table IV); agents 3,845 parameters, 2.8 ms/iteration (Table V); space-complexity formula (pp. 14-15).
openness: none (the Milan demand dataset [36] is only cited as public, p. 12; no code or data link).
q1_support: p. 9: "the wireless channel between the UAV and the ground users is dominated by the line of sight (LoS) link"; ground links use path loss with Rayleigh fading [32] in an own simulator, no 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model.
q2_support: p. 12: "The training set and the test set are divided in a 3:1 ratio"; p. 13: "we conduct a convergence comparison in the scenario where there is an overlap between PU and SU locations"; each scenario is trained, none tests a trained model on unseen conditions.
q3_support: p. 13: "Four comparison schemes are considered for the spectrum sharing performance comparison, namely MAPPO [42], MA2C-DDPG [43], Q learning [30], and Random based scheme [34]"; p. 15: "obtains the highest sum transmission rate of the secondary system among all the considered benchmark schemes".
q4_support: p. 15: "we compare it with the benchmark resource allocation schemes in terms of the number of parameters and computation time required for the forward propagation"; Table V lists 3845 parameters and 2.8 ms/iteration for the proposed scheme.
q5_support: p. 12: "operated on the publicly available dataset [36]"; that dataset holds Milan SMS, call and Internet demand, not channels, and the channels are simulated (p. 9); no code or data link is given.
notes: Included as area 6 (borderline, reviewer to confirm): the learned decisions are sub-band allocation for UAV-to-ground links jointly with UAV trajectory (p. 11), which rule 4 treats as physical layer for aerial links; the demand predictor is traffic prediction used only as agent input. q5 is 0 because the only public data (Milan traffic, p. 12) is the demand of the learning task, not a channel dataset or measured channels; reviewer may check.
